current.text: Reports from Rockets media day say Durant will play fewer minutes this season. The Rockets claim the cut will be significant.

Lloyd does not believe the Rockets will cut his minutes as much as they claim. He expects about 36 minutes, maybe 35, because Ime Udoka plays his starters heavy minutes. If his minutes fall to 33, his value changes materially.
He hurt his ankle in the playoffs but is fine now. His Yahoo status is questionable, marked not injury related.
Fred VanVleet is back. The projected starters are VanVleet, Amen Thompson, Durant, Jabari Smith Jr. and Alperen Sengun. Durant plays forward and will play almost no shooting guard.

In category leagues the experts see him as a late first-round player. Yahoo's rank of 14 to 15 is about right or slight value. His ESPN rank of 28 is far too low, and Lloyd calls him his best Rockets target at that price.
In an auction mock, Josh would bid into the 30s for Durant. He called the 40 USD winning price too rich.
He has the narrowest outcome range in round two: best case 6th, worst case 24th, not counting injury.
At 37 he will probably decline, and he may not stay as healthy after his heavy minutes. One expert expects the Rockets to manage his workload more this season.
With a March 28 end, the Rockets play 3, 3 and 4 games in our fantasy playoff weeks, 10 games in total, which is weak. They have only 14 back-to-backs this season.
The Rockets are projected to win 54 games. They are expected to be conservative in the regular season and not chase seeding.

durable.text: Durant is an efficient high-volume scorer who shoots well from the field and the line. His points, FG% and FT% are all clearly above the pool, and his blocks are strong for his position. His steals are low.
Turnovers are his one weak category. At about 3 per game, he is a clear outlier against the pool.
The main long-term worry is whether his body holds up, given his age.
He is worth much more in category leagues than in points leagues. Points-league rankings undervalue him for our format.

note: The category-league experts agree that Durant is a late first-round value. His only real hole is turnovers (z -1.7), so he fits punt TO builds best, and his volume shooting helps both FG% and FT%. Prices vary: Yahoo values him at 42 USD with an average cost of 49.6 USD, ESPN at 26 USD, and he went for 44 USD in our league last season. In Josh's mock, 40 USD was already too rich, so a price in the low 40s is fair and the 50 USD range is a stretch. In the first weeks, check whether he plays 35 to 36 minutes or nearer 33, the level where Lloyd says his value changes materially. Also remember the Rockets play only 10 games in our playoff weeks.
